title: Free characteristic, nonunit ideal and parameters in the strict local ring
statement: Let W be an affine locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], with a fine saturated log regular structure N [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let beta be a chart by N^r. For any w and algebraically closed geometric point t above w [def-weil-geometric-point], let J be exactly the nonunit ordinary coordinates, and use the actual functions and increasing list [def-trf-free-log-chart-coordinates]. Then the characteristic at t is multiplicatively isomorphic to N^J, with every chart monomial sent to its restriction to J. The nonunit ideal, transported by the canonical strict-henselization comparison [def-trf-log-etale-restriction-stalk-comparison], is the ideal of the strictCoordinate(j), j in J. The recorded strict henselization is local and Noetherian and the ordered list of these strict coordinates extends to a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters].

source.place: Expose VI, 1.2 and 1.6--1.7, printed pp. 69--70; characteristic faces and descent of free chart parameters, extracted from returned proof steps 7--8.

proof.text: Put $B=\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and $A=B^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Choose a Noetherian affine open around $w$ using local Noetherianity. Its local ring $B$ is a localization by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], hence is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Write this open as $\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $\mathfrak p\subset D$ for the prime of $w$, so $B=D_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] the pointed-neighbourhood ring $A$ of $\bar w$ is isomorphic as a $D$-algebra, compatibly with the structural morphism, to an algebraic strict henselization of $B$ relative to the separable closure $l$ of $\kappa(w)$ in $\Omega$, and its residue field is identified with $l$. Through this identification the ring-level strict-henselization lemmas below and in step 5 apply to $A$ and to the canonical map $B\to A$. Then $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. The structural map $B\to A$ is local by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]; therefore a $t_i$ is a unit in $B$ iff it is a unit in $A$ (units map to units, and nonunits lie in the maximal ideal, whose image lies in the target maximal ideal). In particular the same set $J$ indexes the nonunits in both rings.

source.place: Tags 06LJ (lemma-henselization-noetherian), 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization); affine localizations: schemes.tex Tag 01HV, algebra.tex Tag 00FN.

proof.text: Write $K=\{1,\ldots,r\}\setminus J$. A monomial $t^a$ is a unit iff every factor with positive exponent is a unit: if $uv$ has inverse $z$, then $u$ has inverse $vz$. Hence the preimage of $A^\times$ in $\mathbf N^r$ is $\mathbf N^K$. The chart pushout of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] is explicitly $\mathbf N^J\oplus A^\times$: its forward map sends $[(a_J,a_K),u]$ to $(a_J,t_K^{a_K}u)$ and its inverse sends $(a_J,u)$ to $[(a_J,0),u]$. These are inverse by the pushout relation. Quotienting by units gives the canonical characteristic $\mathbf N^J$. A log element is a nonunit precisely when $a_J\ne0$. Its structural image $u\prod_{j\in J}t_j^{a_j}$ lies in $(t_j:j\in J)A$, and each $t_j$ is itself such an image. Thus the nonunit ideal is exactly $I=(t_j:j\in J)A$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1--1.2, printed p. 69; explicit associated-log-stalk pushout for the free chart.

proof.text: By log regularity, $A/I$ is regular local and $\dim A=\dim(A/I)+|J|$, since $(\mathbf N^J)^{\mathrm{gp}}=\mathbf Z^J$. Choose a regular system of parameters $\bar b_1,\ldots,\bar b_s$ of $A/I$, where $s=\dim(A/I)$, and lift them to $b_i\in\mathfrak m_A$. Such a system exists by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$, taking inverse images of the equality $\mathfrak m_A/I=(\bar b_1,\ldots,\bar b_s)$ gives $\mathfrak m_A=(t_j:j\in J)+(b_1,\ldots,b_s)$. This list has $|J|+s=\dim A$ entries and generates the maximal ideal, so by the definitions it is a regular system of parameters and $A$ is regular. This uses the given $t_j$, in their indexed order, without replacing them by associates.

lean.statement:
theorem freeLogChart_strict_parameters
    (W : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine W] [IsLocallyNoetherian W]
    (N : EtaleLogStructure W) (hfs : N.IsFineSaturated)
    (hlog : FineSaturatedLogScheme.IsLogRegular ⟨W, inferInstance, N, hfs⟩)
    (r : ℕ) (β : Multiplicative (ULift.{u} (Fin r) → ℕ) →*
      N.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 W))))
    (hβ : N.IsChart (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 W)) β)
    (w : W) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ W) (ht : (Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField Ω W t).1 = w) :
      (∃ E : N.characteristic t ≃*
          Multiplicative ({i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) //
            ¬ IsUnit (FreeLogChart.ordinaryCoordinate N β w i)} → ℕ),
        ∀ a : Multiplicative (ULift.{u} (Fin r) → ℕ),
          E (Associates.mk (N.toEtalePrelogStructure.germ t
            (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 W)) (CategoryTheory.Over.homMk t (by simp)) (β a))) =
            Multiplicative.ofAdd (fun j ↦ a.toAdd j.val)) ∧
      (N.nonunitIdeal t).map (strictLocalRingStrictHenselizationIso W t).hom.hom =
        Ideal.span {a | ∃ i : ULift.{u} (Fin r),
          ¬ IsUnit (FreeLogChart.ordinaryCoordinate N β w i) ∧
            a = FreeLogChart.strictCoordinate N β t i} ∧
      (∃ (_ : IsLocalRing (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing t))
          (_ : IsNoetherianRing (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing t)),
        (∃ b : List (Scheme.strictHenselizationRing t),
          IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters
            (((FreeLogChart.nonunitIndices N β w).map
              (FreeLogChart.strictCoordinate N β t)) ++ b)))
